get.summary: List parcels, newest change first.
get.description: Pages of `limit` parcels (default 500), from `offset`. A full page carries the `X-Next-Offset` header with the offset of the next page; the last page has none. `q` keeps parcels in which every word appears in the tracking number, label, carrier, status, the carrier's status text, an item name, or the order's shop, number or name. `sort` (default `-updated_at`): `updated_at`, `name` (label, else item names in that label mode, else tracking number), `status`, `lookup`, `carrier` or `expected`; a leading `-` sorts descending, parcels without a value come last.

get.summary: List orders with their items and parcels, newest first.
get.description: An order's `status` is derived from its parcels: `ordered` (nothing shipped yet), `partly_shipped`, `shipped`, `partly_delivered`, `delivered`, or `problem` (a parcel not yet delivered reports a problem or is returning); and from the shop's emails: `cancelled` (nothing of it arrived), `refunded` (money back without a return), and for an order without parcels `shipped` or `delivered` as the shop reports it. `digital` orders (shops of digital goods) are delivered when bought. Cancelled and refunded orders are archived. Archiving is automatic (`archive_mode: automatic`): an order is archived once all its parcels are archived, and parcels archive themselves after the retention window (`archiveAfterDays`) once delivered; an order that never got a parcel is archived 30 days after it was placed. The owner can archive by hand (`archived`) or keep an order out of the archive (`kept`). `view`: `open` (default; not delivered, not archived), `delivered` (all parcels delivered, not archived), `archived`, or `all`. Pages of `limit` orders (default 100) from `offset`; when another page follows, the response carries the `X-Next-Offset` header.

return_by.description: The last local day to hand the return in.

cost.description: What sending it back costs; null when not known.

get.summary: List returns, newest first.
get.description: A return is something sent back to a shop, per order. Connections (a shop account, return and refund mails) create and update it; `status` goes `requested`, `label_created`, `dropped_off`, `in_transit`, `received`, `refunded`, or ends `rejected` or `cancelled`. A return not handed in by `return_by` (the server's local day) reads `expired`. `drop_off` lists where it may be handed in (`kind`: `shop`, `parcel_locker`, `post_office`, `pickup`, or `any` point of the carrier); `cost` says whether sending it back is free. Once a tracking number is known, `parcel_id` is the outgoing parcel that tracks it. Returns hide while every connection that reported them, or their order, is disabled. Changes fire `return.created` and `return.updated`. `view`: `open` (default; still going on), `closed` (refunded, rejected, cancelled or expired), or `all`.

return_by.description: The last local day to hand the return in.

cost.description: What sending it back costs; null when not known.

Redacted state of connections, parcels, live tracking and unknown carrier values.
Server-Sent Events stream of live events about parcels, orders and connections.
get.description: Each message carries `id` (the outbox sequence), `event` (the live event type) and JSON `data`. Reconnect with `Last-Event-ID` (or `?last_event_id=`) to replay up to 24 hours of missed live events. A stream without one starts with `ready` (its `id` is the current sequence). When the given id is newer than any event or older than what is kept, `resync` (also carrying the current sequence as `id`) tells the client to reload everything over REST. `parcel.live_position` messages carry the courier's position while on the road until the delivery ends: `parcel_id`, `latitude`, `longitude`, `accuracy`, `position_at` and `stops_away`; they have no `id` and are never replayed.

parameters.name: access_token
parameters.description: A login's access token (`POST /api/v1/logins`), for clients that cannot send headers (browsers' EventSource). API tokens go in the Authorization header only.

get.summary: Everything that changed after a cursor, deletions included (docs/sync.md).
get.description: Without `since` (or with `0`) the first page of everything. Each answer carries `cursor`; while `more` is true, call again at once with it, then later to pick up new changes. Parcels come without `history`: their events are listed under `events`. `410 sync_expired`: the cursor is older than the kept deletions (90 days) or newer than the server's data (restored from a backup); drop the copy and sync from the start.

cursor.description: Pass as `since` on the next call. Opaque: never compute with it.

more.description: Another page follows at once: call again with `cursor`.

return_by.description: The last local day to hand the return in.
